title: Computing 1980–1989
source: Generated from “Timeline of computing 1980–1989” on Wikipedia; each event links to its source article.

events.title: On April 2 PS/2 Systems were introduced by IBM
events.text: On April 2 PS/2 Systems were introduced by IBM. The first 4 models were released on this date. The PS/2 Model 30 based on an 8086 processor and an old XT bus, Models 50 and 60 based on the 80286 processor and the Model 80 based on the 80386 processor

events.title: OS/2 Launched by Microsoft and IBM
events.text: OS/2 Launched by Microsoft and IBM. A later enhancement, OS/2 Warp provided many of the 32 bit enhancements boasted by Windows 95but several years earlier, yet the product failed to dominate the market in the way Windows 95 did 8 years later.

events.title: The 8514/A introduced by IBM
events.text: The 8514/A introduced by IBM. This was a graphics card that included its own processor to speed up the drawing of common objects. The advantages included a reduction in CPU workload.

events.title: VGA released (designed for the PS/2) by IBM
events.text: VGA released (designed for the PS/2) by IBM.

events.title: 80386SX was released as a cheaper alternative to the 80386DX
events.text: 80386SX was released as a cheaper alternative to the 80386DX. It had a narrower (16 bit) time multiplexed bus. This reduction in pins, and the easier integration with 16 bit devices, made the cost savings. (US)

events.title: Adobe Photoshop software created
events.text: Adobe Photoshop software created.

events.title: Common Access Method committee (CAM) formed
events.text: Common Access Method committee (CAM) formed. They invented the ATA standard in March 1989.

events.title: EISA Bus standard introduced
events.text: EISA Bus standard introduced.

events.title: First optical chip developed, it uses light instead of electricity to
events.text: First optical chip developed, it uses light instead of electricity to increase processing speed.

events.title: Foundation of the MPEG group by Leonardo Chiariglione and Hiroshi Yasu
events.text: Foundation of the MPEG group by Leonardo Chiariglione and Hiroshi Yasuda. (Italy)

events.title: IBM PS/2 Model 30 286 released, based on an 80286 processor and the ol
events.text: IBM PS/2 Model 30 286 released, based on an 80286 processor and the old AT busIBM abandoned the MCA bus, released less than 18 months earlier. Other IBM machines continued to use the MCA bus. (US)

events.title: Macintosh IIx released
events.text: Macintosh IIx released. It was based on a new processor, the Motorola 68030. It still ran at 16 MHz but now achieved 3.9 MIPS. It could be expanded to 128 MB of RAM and had 6 NuBus expansions slots.

events.text: MS-DOS 4.01, PC DOS 4.01 (US)

events.title: PC DOS 4
events.text: PC DOS 4.0, MS-DOS 4.0 (US)

events.text: WORM (Write Once Read Many times)disks marketed for first time by IBM.

events.title: XMS Standard introduced
events.text: XMS Standard introduced.

events.title: 80486DX released by Intel
events.text: 80486DX released by Intel. It contains the equivalent of about 1.2 million transistors. At the time of release the fastest version ran at 25 MHz and achieved up to 20 MIPS. (US)

events.title: Apple Computer released Macintosh SE/30
events.text: Apple Computer released Macintosh SE/30. Like the SE of March 1987 it only had a monochrome display adapter but was fitted with the newer 68030 processor. (US)

events.text: Lotus Notes software launched.

events.title: Open Architecture System Integration Strategy is presented by Apple Co
events.text: Open Architecture System Integration Strategy is presented by Apple Computer as the philosophy behind the Mac in marketing beginning in 1989.

events.title: Release of Sound Blaster Card, by Creative Labs, its success was ensur
events.text: Release of Sound Blaster Card, by Creative Labs, its success was ensured by maintaining compatibility with the widely supported AdLib soundcard of 1987. (Singapore)

events.title: The Macintosh IIcx released, with the same basic capabilities of the M
events.text: The Macintosh IIcx released, with the same basic capabilities of the Macintosh IIx but in a more compact half-width case. (US)

events.title: The Video Electronics Standards Association, an industry consortium of
events.text: The Video Electronics Standards Association, an industry consortium of major SVGA card manufacturers, was formed and introduced the VESA BIOS Extensions standard. (US)

events.title: Tim Berners-Lee submitted a memorandum, titled "Information Management
events.text: Tim Berners-Lee submitted a memorandum, titled "Information Management: A Proposal" to the management at CERN. The proposal talks of "... a "web" of notes with links (like references) between them ...". (Switzerland)
